section: SC/ST rights - Articles 15, 16, 17, 46, 164, 244, 330, 332, 335; abolition of untouchability
subsections: Sub-classification of SCs - Madiga Dandora, Usha Mehra, Davinder Singh
Social movements against untouchability in Andhra

accepted.s: The Madiga Dandora movement, launched by the Madiga Reservation Porata Samithi (MRPS) in 1994, was primarily associated with which demand?
o: Creation of a separate State for Dalits
Abolition of the entire reservation system for Scheduled Castes
Reservation of seats exclusively for Scheduled Tribes
A-B-C-D categorisation of Scheduled Castes in Andhra Pradesh
accepted.x: Madiga Dandora, led by Manda Krishna Madiga through MRPS, demanded A-B-C-D categorisation and a separate share within the Scheduled Caste quota in Andhra Pradesh.
accepted.tq: Identify the precise demand associated with a social movement.
accepted.sec: Sub-classification of SCs - Madiga Dandora, Usha Mehra, Davinder Singh

accepted.s: Who led the Madiga Dandora movement?
accepted.x: The Madiga Dandora movement was led by Manda Krishna Madiga of the Madiga Reservation Porata Samithi.
accepted.tq: Direct person–movement identification.
accepted.sec: Sub-classification of SCs - Madiga Dandora, Usha Mehra, Davinder Singh

accepted.s: The Madiga Dandora movement alleged that which community dominated the 15 per cent Scheduled Caste quota?
accepted.x: The movement alleged that the Mala community disproportionately dominated the 15 per cent Scheduled Caste quota, leading to the demand for a separate share.
accepted.tq: Discriminate between closely related communities in a reservation controversy.
accepted.sec: Sub-classification of SCs - Madiga Dandora, Usha Mehra, Davinder Singh

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the Justice P. Ramachandra Raju Commission:
1. It recommended grouping the Scheduled Castes of Andhra Pradesh into four categories.
2. The four categories were designated A, B, C and D.
3. It recommended grouping Madigas under Category B and Malas under Category C.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: All three statements are correct. The Commission recommended four groups: A comprising Relli and others, B Madiga, C Mala and D Adi-Andhra.
accepted.tq: Check the complete composition of a classification rather than recognising only its headline.
accepted.sec: Sub-classification of SCs - Madiga Dandora, Usha Mehra, Davinder Singh

accepted.s: Which one of the following correctly describes the sequence associated with Scheduled Caste sub-classification in Andhra Pradesh?
o: Justice Ramachandra Raju Commission — 1996; AP SC Rationalisation Act — 2000
Justice Ramachandra Raju Commission — 2000; AP SC Rationalisation Act — 1996
Usha Mehra Commission — 1996; AP SC Rationalisation Act — 2004
Davinder Singh judgment — 2000; AP SC Rationalisation Act — 2024
accepted.x: The Justice P. Ramachandra Raju Commission made its recommendation in 1996, and the AP SC (Rationalisation of Reservations) Act was enacted in 2000.
accepted.tq: Use the date sequence to separate a commission recommendation from the later legislation.
accepted.sec: Sub-classification of SCs - Madiga Dandora, Usha Mehra, Davinder Singh

accepted.s: Which State was the first to sub-categorise Scheduled Castes after the Justice Ramachandra Raju Commission process?
accepted.x: Andhra Pradesh became the first State to sub-categorise Scheduled Castes through the AP SC (Rationalisation of Reservations) Act, 2000.
accepted.tq: Test a superlative linked to a specific legislative milestone.
accepted.sec: Sub-classification of SCs - Madiga Dandora, Usha Mehra, Davinder Singh

accepted.s:
With reference to E.V. Chinnaiah v. State of Andhra Pradesh, consider the following statements:
1. The Supreme Court treated Scheduled Castes as a single homogeneous class under Article 341.
2. It struck down the Andhra Pradesh Scheduled Caste (Rationalisation of Reservations) Act, 2000.
3. It held that sub-classification did not interfere with the Presidential list under Article 341.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Chinnaiah treated Scheduled Castes as a homogeneous class and struck down the State Act; it regarded sub-classification as interfering with the Article 341 list, so statement 3 is false.
accepted.tq: Find the statement that reverses the court’s holding.
accepted.sec: Sub-classification of SCs - Madiga Dandora, Usha Mehra, Davinder Singh

accepted.s: The Usha Mehra Commission, constituted in 2007–08, recommended which of the following?
o: Amending Article 341 to enable States to sub-categorise Scheduled Castes
Including all Other Backward Classes in the Scheduled Caste list
accepted.x: The Usha Mehra Commission recommended amendment of Article 341 so that States could undertake sub-categorisation of Scheduled Castes.
accepted.tq: Match a commission with its specific recommendation.
accepted.sec: Sub-classification of SCs - Madiga Dandora, Usha Mehra, Davinder Singh

accepted.s: In State of Punjab v. Davinder Singh (2024), the seven-judge Bench held that sub-classification within Scheduled Castes is permissible when the class is not homogeneous. What was the majority ratio?
accepted.x: The seven-judge Bench permitted sub-classification by a majority of 6:1, overruling the position taken in E.V. Chinnaiah.
accepted.tq: Test the exact judicial majority using closely spaced numerical distractors.
accepted.sec: Sub-classification of SCs - Madiga Dandora, Usha Mehra, Davinder Singh

accepted.s: Which one of the following is NOT correctly matched?
o: Usha Mehra Commission — Amendment of Article 341 recommended
Davinder Singh case — Sub-classification within Scheduled Castes permitted
Indra Sawhney case — Sub-classification of Scheduled Castes in Andhra Pradesh upheld
E.V. Chinnaiah case — Scheduled Castes treated as a homogeneous class
accepted.x: Indra Sawhney dealt principally with reservation under Article 16(4), the 50 per cent ceiling and reservation at initial appointment; it did not uphold Andhra Pradesh’s Scheduled Caste sub-classification.
accepted.tq: Eliminate the option that assigns a later State-specific issue to an unrelated case.
accepted.sec: Sub-classification of SCs - Madiga Dandora, Usha Mehra, Davinder Singh

accepted.s:
Consider the following pairs:
1. Indra Sawhney — Reservation under Article 16(4) only at initial appointment
2. M. Nagaraj — Requirement of quantifiable data concerning backwardness, inadequate representation and administrative efficiency
3. Jarnail Singh — Data on backwardness of Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes necessary for promotion reservation
Which of the pairs given above are correctly matched?
accepted.x: Pairs 1 and 2 are correctly matched. Jarnail Singh held that data on backwardness was not required for Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes in this context, making pair 3 incorrect.
accepted.tq: Separate similar reservation judgments by their distinct holdings.
accepted.sec: Sub-classification of SCs - Madiga Dandora, Usha Mehra, Davinder Singh

accepted.s: Which case upheld the 77th, 81st, 82nd and 85th Constitutional Amendments, subject to the State showing quantifiable data on specified conditions?
o: State of Punjab v. Davinder Singh
Jarnail Singh v. Lachhmi Narain Gupta
M. Nagaraj v. Union of India
E.V. Chinnaiah v. State of Andhra Pradesh
accepted.x: M. Nagaraj upheld the four constitutional amendments but required quantifiable data concerning backwardness, inadequate representation and administrative efficiency.
accepted.tq: Associate a cluster of constitutional amendments with the case that examined them.
accepted.sec: Sub-classification of SCs - Madiga Dandora, Usha Mehra, Davinder Singh

accepted.s: Which State became the first to implement Scheduled Caste sub-categorisation after the Davinder Singh judgment?
accepted.x: Telangana became the first State to implement Scheduled Caste sub-categorisation after Davinder Singh, with three groups in April 2025.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the State that enacted the earlier framework from the State that implemented the post-2024 classification.
accepted.sec: Sub-classification of SCs - Madiga Dandora, Usha Mehra, Davinder Singh

accepted.s: The first Dalit organisation in Hyderabad State was established by Bhagya Reddy Varma under the name
accepted.x: Bhagya Reddy Varma established Jagan Mitra Mandali in 1906, described as the first Dalit organisation in Hyderabad State.
accepted.tq: Match the organisation with its founder and year.
accepted.sec: Social movements against untouchability in Andhra

accepted.s: Bhagya Reddy Varma’s Adi Hindu Social Service League, established in 1911, was originally known as
accepted.x: The Adi Hindu Social Service League was originally called Manya Sangham before being established under its later name in 1911.
accepted.tq: Discriminate between an organisation’s original and later names.
accepted.sec: Social movements against untouchability in Andhra

accepted.s: The Adi-Andhra movement of the 1910s–1930s was based on the claim that Dalits were
o: Exclusively agricultural labourers without a distinct identity
Recent migrants to Andhra from Maharashtra
Members of the ruling dynasty of Andhra
accepted.x: The Adi-Andhra movement asserted that Dalits were the original inhabitants of Andhra and demanded access to education, temples and tanks.
accepted.tq: Identify the ideological claim underlying a regional social movement.
accepted.sec: Social movements against untouchability in Andhra

accepted.s: Which of the following demands was associated with the Adi-Andhra movement?
o: Access to education, temples and tanks
Abolition of all local self-government institutions
Replacement of public schools by religious institutions
Exclusive control over village revenue offices
accepted.x: The Adi-Andhra movement demanded access for Dalits to education, temples and tanks.
accepted.tq: Link a movement with its concrete social demands.
accepted.sec: Social movements against untouchability in Andhra

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements:
1. Gandhi used the term ‘Harijan’.
2. B.R. Ambedkar preferred the terms ‘Dalit’ and ‘Scheduled Caste’ and emphasised legal-constitutional remedies.
3. Bhagya Reddy Varma supported the Harijan Sevak Sangh without criticism.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Bhagya Reddy Varma criticised the Harijan Sevak Sangh as paternalistic, making statement 3 incorrect.
accepted.tq: Use the contrasting approaches of major reformers and identify the reversed statement.
accepted.sec: Social movements against untouchability in Andhra

accepted.s: Vaikom Satyagraha of 1924–25 was primarily associated with the demand for
o: Entry into the Kalaram temple at Nashik
The right to draw water from Mahad tank
The right of lower castes to use roads around the Vaikom temple
accepted.x: Vaikom Satyagraha in Travancore demanded the right of lower castes to use the roads surrounding the Vaikom temple.
accepted.tq: Distinguish similar anti-untouchability movements by place and immediate objective.
accepted.sec: Social movements against untouchability in Andhra

accepted.s: Which one of the following combinations relating to Vaikom Satyagraha is correct?
o: Travancore — T.K. Madhavan and Keshava Menon — 1924–25
accepted.x: Vaikom Satyagraha took place in Travancore in 1924–25 and was organised by T.K. Madhavan and Keshava Menon, with K. Kelappan also associated with it.
accepted.tq: Start with the sure location and verify the corresponding leaders and date.
accepted.sec: Social movements against untouchability in Andhra

accepted.s: Which leader was jailed in connection with the Vaikom Satyagraha?
accepted.x: Periyar was jailed during the Vaikom Satyagraha. Sree Narayana Guru supported the movement.
accepted.tq: Test the individual role within a multi-leader movement.
accepted.sec: Social movements against untouchability in Andhra

Match List-I with List-II:

List-I (Movement)
a. Mahad Satyagraha
b. Manusmriti Dahan
c. Kalaram Temple Entry
 d. Guruvayur Satyagraha

Select the correct answer using the code below:

accepted.tq: Start from the distinctive date or place and complete the matching code.

accepted.s: The Mahad Chavdar Tank Satyagraha was led by B.R. Ambedkar to assert the right of Dalits to
o: Draw water from a public tank
Use roads around the Vaikom temple
accepted.x: The Mahad Satyagraha, held at Mahad in Maharashtra on 20 March 1927, asserted Dalits’ right to draw water from the public Chavdar Tank.
accepted.tq: Identify a movement from its precise immediate objective.
accepted.sec: Social movements against untouchability in Andhra

accepted.s: The centenary observance of the Mahad Chavdar Tank Satyagraha began on
accepted.x: The centenary observance of the 20 March 1927 Mahad Satyagraha began on 20 March 2026.
accepted.tq: Separate the original event date from the beginning of its centenary observance.
accepted.sec: Social movements against untouchability in Andhra

accepted.s: Who led the Kalaram Temple Entry movement at Nashik in 1930?
accepted.x: B.R. Ambedkar led the Kalaram Temple Entry movement at Nashik in 1930 with 15,000 volunteers.
accepted.tq: Associate a leader with a specific temple-entry movement.
accepted.sec: Social movements against untouchability in Andhra

accepted.s: The Harijan Sevak Sangh was established in 1932 after the Poona Pact and was associated with which publication, begun in 1933?
accepted.x: Gandhi associated the Harijan Sevak Sangh with the paper Harijan, which began publication in 1933.
accepted.tq: Link an organisation with its associated publication and timeline.
accepted.sec: Social movements against untouchability in Andhra

accepted.s: Which one of the following is correctly matched?
accepted.x: The Siddhantam Temple Entry movement took place in Krishna district in 1933 and was one of the earliest such movements in Andhra. The other options confuse its details with those of other movements.
accepted.tq: Check location and date together to expose swapped movement details.
accepted.sec: Social movements against untouchability in Andhra

accepted.s: The Siddhantam Temple Entry movement of 1933 was organised mainly by
accepted.x: The Siddhantam Temple Entry movement in Krishna district was organised by Congress and Gandhian leaders.
accepted.tq: Identify the organisational leadership behind a regional movement.
accepted.sec: Social movements against untouchability in Andhra

accepted.s: The Safai Karmachari Andolan is principally a campaign against
accepted.x: The Safai Karmachari Andolan campaigns against manual scavenging and is associated with Bezwada Wilson.
accepted.tq: Match a movement with its central social issue.
accepted.sec: Social movements against untouchability in Andhra

accepted.s: Bezwada Wilson received the Ramon Magsaysay Award in which year?
accepted.x: Bezwada Wilson, associated with the Safai Karmachari Andolan, received the Ramon Magsaysay Award in 2016.
accepted.tq: Test a precise award year using nearby chronological distractors.

accepted.s: Which one of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
o: Jagan Mitra Mandali — Bhagya Reddy Varma
Harijan Sevak Sangh — Manda Krishna Madiga
accepted.x: The Harijan Sevak Sangh was associated with Gandhi, whereas Manda Krishna Madiga led the Madiga Dandora movement.
accepted.tq: Use a nearby movement leader as the distractor and identify the swapped association.

accepted.s: Gurram Jashuva’s Gabbilam is based on the idea that
o: A bat can enter a temple while an untouchable cannot
A king grants land to temple servants
A crow carries a message from Buddha to an emperor
A temple priest abolishes caste through ritual
accepted.x: In Gabbilam, an untouchable labourer sends his plea to Lord Shiva through a bat because the bat may enter the temple while he may not.
accepted.tq: Test the central image and social contrast in a literary work.
accepted.sec: Literature against untouchability → author

accepted.s: Gabbilam, written by Gurram Jashuva in 1941, was modelled on which work of Kalidasa?
accepted.x: Gurram Jashuva’s Gabbilam was modelled on Kalidasa’s Meghaduta.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the literary model from other works by the same author.
accepted.sec: Literature against untouchability → author

accepted.s: Which one of the following works was written by Jyotiba Phule?
accepted.x: Jyotiba Phule wrote Gulamgiri, published in 1873, in which caste oppression was compared with American slavery.
accepted.tq: Direct author–work recall with closely related anti-caste literature as distractors.

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements:
1. Annihilation of Caste was written by B.R. Ambedkar.
2. Who Were the Shudras? and The Untouchables were also written by B.R. Ambedkar.
3. Nimna Jatula Charitra was written by Ambedkar.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Nimna Jatula Charitra was written by Jala Rangaswamy, not B.R. Ambedkar.
accepted.tq: Catch the wrong author assigned to a similar anti-caste title.

accepted.s: Which one of the following is correctly matched?
accepted.x: Nimna Jatula Charitra was written by Jala Rangaswamy. Adi Andhra was associated with Didla Pullaiah, Nava Jeevan with Undru Subbarao, and Gabbilam with Gurram Jashuva.
accepted.tq: Separate literary works from Andhra Dalit newspapers and detect swapped authors.
accepted.sec: Literature against untouchability → author

accepted.s: Which of the following pairs relating to Andhra Dalit newspapers is correct?
accepted.x: Adi Andhra was associated with Didla Pullaiah, while Nava Jeevan was associated with Undru Subbarao.
accepted.tq: Discriminate between two similar newspaper–editor associations.
